solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Take on equipment

definitions.meaning: to take on an opponent is to confront or challenge them
gear or kit, especially for fishing

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to handle a job's gear, or to take on extra kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a challenge in sport or argument, and fishing gear or general kit.

clue.text: Complete, from beginning to end, nothing concealed

indicators.note: the zero is hidden away inside the longer word, so it is a container signal

parts.note: going all the way from start to finish is going through
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A report claims to be total, start to finish, with nothing hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough job is a complete one, with every detail covered.

clue.text: Roasted food item — when ready, we served up on crackers, mostly

parts.note: ready money, or 'the ready', is cash

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word goes upwards, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: crackers means mad, as does nuts

explanation.surface: A cook tells guests a roasted snack is coming once it is ready, served on crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns WE into EW; 'mostly' drops the S from NUTS. 'when' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: This kidney-shaped kernel is commonly sold roasted as a snack.

clue.text: In hotel I study register

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: A guest studies the register in a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A register is a list of names or items recorded officially.

clue.text: I'd piece prepared about mass outbreak

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, around, the single letter
letters that are prepared are made up afresh, rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as the anagram fodder
m is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Someone has written an article about a widespread outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges IDPIECE into EPIDEIC, which goes 'about' M.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a disease spreading through many people at once.

clue.text: Criticise expert sitting on a universal remedy

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
an ace is someone highly skilled

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a specialist who is relying on a cure-all.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a cure-all, a remedy supposed to heal every ill.

clue.text: Couples who may make one laugh in adult clubs, wearing old padded jackets

definitions.text: Couples who may make one laugh

indicators.note: the jackets are worn by, so wrapped round, the two letters

parts.note: doublets were close-fitting padded jackets worn by men in past centuries
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Comedy duos turn up in clubs dressed in period padded jackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy pairs who perform together on stage are known by this term.

clue.text: Clean head of hair on top

parts.note: a mop is a thick, untidy mass of hair
up means above, on top

explanation.surface: An instruction to wash the hair on the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop up is to clean away spilt liquid or tidy remaining mess.

clue.text: Calling baby-sitter around eight, initially

indicators.note: the minder's word goes around the single letter

parts.note: a carer is someone who looks after another, as a baby-sitter does

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word eight

explanation.surface: Phoning the baby-sitter at around eight o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a vocation, one's chosen profession or line of work.

clue.text: Consent to entertaining mischievous child, one not easily got rid of

definitions.text: one not easily got rid of

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so this is a container signal

parts.note: to consent is to let, to allow
an imp is a naughty little child

explanation.surface: A parent agrees to host a naughty child who then refuses to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellfish clinging to rocks gives its name to a hanger-on who will not leave.

clue.text: Thing old bishop put down before sitting

indicators.note: the first pieces come before the sitting in the answer

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a sitting is a session, a period of meeting

explanation.surface: An elderly bishop is put down for an appointment with the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a thing about something is to have a fixation on it.

clue.text: Superior meal, seconds not required

indicators.note: the letter for seconds is not needed, so it is removed

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: An excellent dinner at which nobody wants second helpings.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper means higher in rank or status, as in the upper classes.

clue.text: Ring writer ready to entertain new ideas

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Phoning an author who is receptive to fresh suggestions.
explanation.definitionFit: An open mind is receptive to new thinking and other views.

clue.text: Copy includes song back to front — a major disaster

indicators.note: the copying word takes in the song, a container signal

parts.note: to ape is to imitate or copy

indicators.note: the final letter of the song moves from the back to the front

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean song

explanation.surface: A cover version of a song played backwards turns out a total catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' here means only the song's final letter jumps to its start; it is not a full reversal of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocalypse is an event of catastrophic destruction, like the end of the world.

clue.text: Article on demonstrations in border area

parts.note: the is the definite article
protest marches are demonstrations

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece reports on protests in a frontier region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marches is the border country between England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is historically a frontier district, and the plural names the Anglo-Welsh border lands.

clue.text: Report weapons recently stolen

parts.note: guns are weapons
hot goods are stolen ones, still dangerous to handle

explanation.surface: A news story says firearms have just been taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud bang, such as the crack of a firearm going off.

clue.text: Mountain in eastern part of Sahara desert

indicators.note: the eastern, right-hand, end of the word Sahara is kept and its western start dropped

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert or betray them

explanation.surface: A peak said to stand in the east of the great African desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Ararat is the Turkish peak where Noah's Ark is said to have come to rest.

clue.text: A head of state bound to find out

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: bound to happen means certain to happen

explanation.surface: A president is obliged to discover the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain a fact is to discover or establish it for sure.

clue.text: Fidgety? Be more active!

definitions.meaning: read as an instruction, take fewer breaks: do less resting

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for idling and urged to get moving.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into two words, an order to take less rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to sit still is fidgety; split, the word urges less lounging.

clue.text: End of play is completely perplexing

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the close of a day's play is called by this name, after the wooden posts
baffles utterly, as a puzzle defeats a solver

explanation.surface: The way a drama finishes leaves the audience baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the stumps are the wooden posts of the wicket; drawing them ends a day's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket close-of-play term doubles as a verb for baffling someone completely.

clue.text: Group studying ruined remains

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and its parts jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Archaeologists examining wrecked ancient remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small class meeting to discuss and study a topic.

clue.text: Dead skin around base of nail attractive girl describes

definitions.text: Dead skin around base of nail

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw around, so the girl's word encloses the other letters

parts.note: a cutie is an attractive person
C stands for circa, Latin for around

indicators.note: the base of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A pretty woman explains about the dead skin at the bottom of a fingernail.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and wordplay overlap: 'around' and 'base of nail' serve both. 'describes' means draws round.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuticle is the strip of hardened skin at the base of a fingernail.

clue.text: Modest order husband put in

indicators.note: the single letter is placed inside the class word

parts.note: a caste is a social order or class
h is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

explanation.surface: A prim command that a married man should be installed.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and modest, in behaviour, dress or style.

clue.text: A year in rathole provides refuge

indicators.note: the year letter goes inside the squalid dwelling word

parts.note: a rathole is a squalid place, a slum

explanation.surface: Twelve months spent in a squalid hovel at least gives shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or sanctuary granted, especially to refugees.

clue.text: It can still be served on a round plate!

definitions.text: It can still be served on a round plate!

parts.words: It can still be served on a round plate!
parts.note: a joke on shape: this substantial dinner is called square but arrives on a circular dish

explanation.surface: An odd reassurance that food may go on circular crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: The paradox is that a hearty, filling dinner is named for a square shape though plates are round.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearty, filling dinner is called this, a nourishing proper feed.

clue.text: Complete change in direction brought about by socially acceptable act

parts.note: U means upper-class and so socially acceptable, from the old 'U and non-U' usage
a turn is an act or performance in a variety show

explanation.surface: A polite performance causes a total reversal of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: U as in 'U and non-U' was mid-century slang for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnaround of policy is named after the vehicle manoeuvre of swinging back the way one came.

clue.text: Annoying child runs into club

indicators.note: the letter for runs goes into the club word

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A nuisance kid dashes into a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A brat is a badly behaved, irritating child.

clue.text: Stooge satisfied about routine, at last

indicators.note: the full word goes about, around, the single letter

parts.note: fed means having had enough to eat, satisfied

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of the word routine

explanation.surface: A comic's sidekick is happy with the routine in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian's stooge gives the straight lines, known as a feed, for the punchlines.

clue.text: Lake in steep valley, not cold

indicators.note: not cold means the cold letter is removed

parts.note: a clough is a steep-sided valley or ravine in northern English dialect
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A lake lying in a deep ravine is not freezing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lough is the Irish word for a lake or sea inlet, like the Scottish loch.

clue.text: Small number embarrassed entering flat in building in Paris

parts.note: No is the short form of number

indicators.note: the blushing word enters the dull word, a container signal

parts.note: flat means dull or tame
embarrassed people go red

explanation.surface: A few red-faced people go into an apartment in a Parisian block.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the famous Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité in Paris.

clue.text: Office cars to tax

parts.note: Minis are small British cars
to try someone's patience is to tax or strain it

explanation.surface: A government department plans to tax motor vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A ministry is a government department, a public office.

clue.text: Commercial being televised is for the handsome young man

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, an advertisement
a programme being broadcast is on

explanation.surface: A TV advert features a good-looking youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, the youth loved by Aphrodite in Greek myth, stands for any beautiful young man.
